newsitem.title: ITALY: More Italian forces head off for Albania.
newsitem.headline: More Italian forces head off for Albania.

text.p: An Italian amphibious assault ship with around 600 men on board set sail for Albania on Sunday as preparations continued for the multinational security mission to the anarchic country.
Defence officials declined to say when the San Giusto assault ship would arrive but the main bulk of Italy's 2,500 troop contingent was due to reach nearby Albania from Tuesday onwards.
An advance group of about 20 men from an army pioneer regiment arrived in the Balkan state last week to pave the way for the operation.
The Italian units will form the backbone of a 6,000-strong force which has been sanctioned by the United Nations Security Council to protect the distribution of food and medical aid.
Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said in a newspaper interview on Sunday that the soldiers would not remain in Albania for long.
"Europe does not intend to create a protectorate in Albania. We are going there to perform an unrewarding action of international responsibility," he told La Repubblica newspaper.
France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania are taking part in the Italian-led operation. Austria and Denmark are also considering participation.
Two Spanish naval ships carrying around 350 troops arrived in Italy's southeastern port of Brindisi on Sunday ahead of their deployment to Albania.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi paid a flying visit to Albania on Sunday before the operation swung into first gear.
"The mission is called 'Alba' (dawn)," Prodi told a news conference in the southern Albanian city of Vlore. "And this could be the dawn in the history of Albania, the rebirth of Albania," he added.
The former communist country was plunged into near-anarchy last month amid widespread popular anger over the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes.
